page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.cm4.3xlarge is a virtual machine type within the High Clock Speed family, powered by the KVM hypervisor on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with a dedicated 3.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8369HB processor comprising 6 physical cores and 12 vCPUs via two threads per core. Memory capacity is 48.0 GB, resulting in an allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware features include support for AVX-512 extensions (including VNNI and BF16) along with L1d, L2, and L3 cache sizes of 32 KB, 1.0 MB, and 33 MB respectively. The instance provides 4 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth and includes zero dedicated GPUs or bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistence.

Benchmark results place the processor in the middle tier of cloud compute performance across most synthetics. The instance registers a stress-ng score of 1,575.58 for single-core and 12,474.34 for multi-core compute. In Geekbench testing, it posts a single-core score of 1,257.0 and a multi-core score of 6,091.0, alongside compiling throughput of 11,282.0 with Clang. Large-block memory bandwidth sustains 55.6 GB/sec read and 46.36 GB/sec write. In contrast, PassMark physics testing (741.78) and PassMark memory testing (1,777.75) both fall into the bottom 25% distribution. Similarly, large language model inference using a 7B parameter model achieves 17.38 prompt tokens per second and 6.99 generation tokens per second, also in the bottom quartile.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.cm4.3xlarge offers a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio suitable for compute-oriented tasks that require predictable, dedicated clock rates without the expense of specialized hardware accelerators. The absence of bundled local storage lowers base hardware overhead but requires users to budget separately for network storage performance. Workloads that align with this profile include mid-tier relational database hosting, static web serving (benchmarked at 7.8 GB/sec throughput), Redis caching (achieving 11.64 million SET operations per second), Clang software compilation, and general-purpose continuous integration pipelines.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.cm4.3xlarge is a dedicated compute instance from the High Clock Speed family based on the x86_64 architecture and KVM hypervisor. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8369HB processor operating at 3.2 GHz, it provides 6 physical cores, 12 vCPUs, and 48.0 GB of memory, yielding 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not bundle local disk storage or hardware accelerators, and it provides 4 Gbps of baseline networking. Synthetic benchmarks demonstrate consistent mid-tier execution, including 1,575.58 single-core and 12,474.34 multi-core stress-ng performance, alongside 11.64 million Redis SET operations per second and 7.8 GB/sec static web throughput. Lower efficiency is observed on memory-intensive benchmarks and larger language model inference. The configuration suits balanced general-purpose workloads, CI/CD compilation, in-memory caching, and standard database services requiring dedicated vCPU allocation.
